chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the Mudabbir (slave manumitted upon the owner's death), is he from the third (of the bequest)? So he said: 'Yes, and it is for the bequeather to retract [the bequest] during good health or illness, if it was his bequest.'

key_terms.أَنْ يَرْجِع: To retract/revoke: The right to cancel the bequest before death
key_terms.الثُّلُث: The third: The portion of the estate allocated for bequests, distinct from the fixed shares of heirs
key_terms.الْمُدَبَّر: Mudabbir: A slave whose manumission is contingent upon the owner's death
key_terms.لِلْمُوصِي: For the bequeather: The person making the will/bequest

ai.seo_question: Is a Mudabbir counted within the one-third share of bequests in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the status of the 'Mudabbir' (a slave emancipated upon the owner's death), confirming they are counted within the one-third estate share reserved for bequests. It further establishes the owner's right to revoke this specific bequest at any time prior to death, whether in health or illness, highlighting the revocable nature of this specific form of manumission. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between immediate emancipation and deferred manumission regarding estate distribution.
